title: We created you. So why not believe?
subtitle: Your first life is the proof of the second
then: The deniers asked: when we become dust and bones, shall we be raised? Allah replies: {idea}We created you{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains: He created you after you were nothing, so is not the One who began creation more able to bring it back?
now: You look at your own baby photo, or at your child asleep. A few years earlier that person did not exist. {idea}You already happened once, from nothing.{/idea} The second time is not harder.
old: Life after death is hard to believe.
new: My own existence is the evidence that it is possible.
try: Look at your hand for a moment today and say: You made this from nothing.

title: Look at the drop you came from.
subtitle: A question meant to make you think
then: Allah asks the listeners to {idea}look at the semen they emit{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains the question: is it you who makes it settle in the womb and creates life from it, stage after stage? The argument is made personal.
now: The first scan: a tiny flicker on a screen in a dim clinic room, and your heart racing. {idea}No one in that room built that heartbeat.{/idea}
old: Making a baby is just a natural process.
new: Every new life is Allah creating, and I am one of them.
try: Congratulate someone who recently had a baby, or make dua for a couple hoping for one.

title: Is it you who creates it, or is it Us?
subtitle: Taking credit versus giving it
then: The question is direct: {idea}is it you who creates it, or are We the Creator?{/idea} Ibn Kathir's answer is that Allah is the One who does all of it. Parents are the means, not the makers.
now: Parents post the newborn photo with a proud caption. The pride is natural. {trap}But no parent designed a single cell.{/trap} {idea}Gratitude is the honest caption.{/idea}
old: My children, my body, my health are my own work.
new: I am the means. Allah is the Creator.
try: Next time you feel proud of something you have, add quietly: this is from Allah.

title: Death is decreed for all, and Allah is never outrun.
subtitle: Death is equal, and His power is total
then: Allah says {idea}We have decreed death among you{/idea}. Ad-Dahhak said Allah made everyone in the heavens and the earth equal with regard to death. We are not outstripped, Ibn Kathir explains, means He is never unable.
now: Rich or poor, gym or no gym, the hospital corridor holds everyone the same way. {idea}Death is the one equal thing.{/idea} Looking after your health is good, but no one outruns the appointment.
old: With enough care and money, I can stay ahead of death.
new: Death is decreed equally, so I prepare instead of running.
try: Spend five minutes today thinking about one thing you would want to finish before you die.

title: He can remake you in forms you do not know.
subtitle: Resurrection is not limited by our imagination
then: Allah is never unable {idea}to change your shapes on the Day of Resurrection{/idea}, Ibn Kathir explains, and create you in forms you do not know. The listeners could not picture a resurrection. The verse says that is no limit for Allah.
now: Twenty years ago you could not have pictured the phone in your pocket. {trap}What you can't picture is not the edge of what is possible.{/trap} Allah's power is not measured by your imagination.
old: If I can't imagine how resurrection works, it's hard to believe.
new: My imagination is not the limit of Allah's power.
try: When something about faith is hard to picture today, say: Allah is able, and leave it there.

title: You know the first creation. Why not reflect?
subtitle: The memory that answers the doubt
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}you know that Allah created you after you were nothing{/idea}, and gave you hearing, sight and hearts. Will you not remember that the One who made you first is more able to bring you back?
now: You ask for signs while ignoring your own heartbeat, the eyes reading this line, the breath in your chest. {idea}The proof isn't missing. Attention is.{/idea}
old: I'd believe more strongly if I had more evidence.
new: The evidence is my own life. I need to remember it.
try: Take three slow breaths today and remember with each one that you were made.
